response.sql: WITH acct_region AS (SELECT o.account_id, d3.A3 AS region, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM `order` o JOIN disp dp ON dp.account_id = o.account_id AND dp.type = 'OWNER' JOIN client c ON c.client_id = dp.client_id JOIN district d3 ON d3.district_id = c.district_id GROUP BY o.account_id, d3.A3), overall AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM acct_region), diffs AS (SELECT ar.account_id, ar.region, ar.order_count, ar.order_count - (SELECT avg_count FROM overall) AS diff FROM acct_region ar), region_avg AS (SELECT region, AVG(diff) AS region_avg_diff FROM diffs GROUP BY region) SELECT df.account_id, df.region, df.order_count, df.diff, df.diff - ra.region_avg_diff AS excess_over_region_avg FROM diffs df JOIN region_avg ra ON ra.region = df.region WHERE df.diff > ra.region_avg_diff ORDER BY excess_over_region_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Standing orders are the rows of the `order` table, and each order is counted once per account–region pair (COUNT DISTINCT order_id guards against duplicate counting if an account has more than one OWNER disposition).
The owner is the disp row with type 'OWNER', and the region comes from that client's home district (client.district_id → district.A3), not the account's branch district (account.district_id).
